description: Settling a child's injury claim in Georgia: when court approval or a conservatorship is required, and strategies to minimize court involvement.
shortAnswer: So long as there is a natural guardian, no court involvement is required on child injury claims that settle for $25,000.00 or less. Natural guardians may also settle claims when the gross amount exceeds $25,000.00 but the net amount to be recovered is less than $25,000.00; however, court approval of the settlement is required.

faq.q: Who is a child's natural guardian for settling an injury claim in Georgia?
faq.a: Georgia law provides that each parent of a minor is a natural guardian, except that, if the parents are divorced and one parent has sole legal custody of the minor, that parent is the sole natural guardian. If the divorced parents have joint legal custody, they both remain natural guardians.

faq.q: Can parents do whatever they want with a child's injury settlement of $25,000 or less in Georgia?
faq.a: No. You have a legal and moral obligation to hold and use all of that sum for the benefit of your child and you can be held legally accountable if you ignore those obligations. See O.C.G.A. Section 29-3-1(b).

faq.q: How can a structured settlement help avoid a conservatorship for a child's settlement?
faq.a: A structured settlement is one way of reducing the "net amount to be recovered" to $25,000.00 or under. If you can, you still have to petition the court for approval of the settlement but no conservatorship is required. The down side of a structured settlement is that there is less (or no) cash up front.

faq.q: What does a conservatorship over a child's settlement involve in Georgia?
faq.a: A conservatorship means the court is in charge of your child's money and your role (if you are appointed to be the conservator) is to carry out the court's directions. Your duties will include preparing and filing an inventory and an asset management plan, annual returns (accounting), tax returns, and petitions for leave to encroach.
